title: Braid relation for the pinned simple-reflection lifts
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and let $P=(G,T=D_A(M),\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\Delta,(X_\alpha))$ be a pinned split realization [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. For $\alpha\in\Delta$, use the canonical exponentials and unique linked opposite generator $Y_{-\alpha}$ of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], and put
$$n_\alpha=\exp_\alpha(X_\alpha)\exp_{-\alpha}(-Y_{-\alpha})\exp_\alpha(X_\alpha)\in G(A).$$
For distinct $a,b\in\Delta$, let $m$ be the order of $s_as_b$ on $M$, where $s_\alpha(v)=v-\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$. Define $A_m$ and $B_m$ to be the alternating words of length $m$ in $n_a,n_b$ starting with $n_a$ and $n_b$, respectively. Then $A_m=B_m$ in $G(A)$. The same equality holds after every ring base change. The assertion includes disconnected and nonreduced bases and all central tori; it is an equality of the pinned lifts themselves, not just of their images in the Weyl group.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-small-centralizer-hom-amalgamation] with $J=\{a,b\}$. Its subgroup $G_J$ retains the full torus, coroots and pinning and has semisimple rank two. By [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] its root exponentials, linked opposite generators and $n_a,n_b$ are those in $G$. It suffices to prove the equality in $G_J(A)$. Relabel so $a$ is short when lengths differ; the desired equality is symmetric under exchanging the labels. Apply [lem-sfb-rank-two-root-string-seed-calculus] to $G_J$. Its four positive-root lists force the following Cartan entries and orders:
$$\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{type}&A_1\times A_1&A_2&B_2&G_2\\ \langle b,a^\vee\rangle&0&-1&-2&-3\\ \langle a,b^\vee\rangle&0&-1&-1&-1\\ m&2&3&4&6.\end{array}$$
For the entries, substitute each listed root into $s_r(v)=v-\langle v,r^\vee\rangle r$: preservation of the lists forces the displayed integers. On $V=\mathbf Qa+\mathbf Qb$ the matrices are $s_a=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-1&-\langle b,a^\vee\rangle\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $s_b=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\-\langle a,b^\vee\rangle&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$; their product has the indicated exact order by multiplication. This is also its order on $M$: the Cartan determinants are $4,3,2,1$, so $M_{\mathbf Q}=V\oplus(\ker a^\vee\cap\ker b^\vee)$, with the reflections trivial on the second summand; $M\hookrightarrow M_{\mathbf Q}$.

proof.text: We need only these no-sum commutations: in $A_1\times A_1$, $U_b$ commutes with $U_a$ and $U_{-a}$; in $B_2$, $U_d$ commutes with $U_b,U_{-b}$, where $d=2a+b$; in $G_2$, $U_f$ commutes with $U_a,U_{-a}$, where $f=3a+2b$. Here is a direct application of the cited statements, including their positivity hypothesis. For each pair $(r,s)$ just named, the lists of [lem-sfb-rank-two-root-string-seed-calculus], together with their negatives, contain no $ir+js$ with $i,j>0$. Indeed in $B_2$ such a combination has coordinates $(2i,i\pm j)$ and in $G_2$ it has coordinates $(3i\pm j,2i)$, neither in the relevant root list; the disconnected case is immediate. Thus $\{r,s\}$ is closed and has no opposite pair. By [lem-sfb-closed-root-set-positive-functional] choose an integral functional positive on this pair and nonzero on every root. Its positive set $\Sigma$ is closed and disjoint from its negative. [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] gives the product-coordinate subgroup for every enumeration of $\Sigma$. Choose generators for its root modules (and all remaining root modules); their canonical exponentials satisfy the closed-immersion, tangent and equivariance hypotheses of [lem-sfb-equivariant-root-commutator-support]. That node's empty-index-set clause now gives each asserted commutation as an identity on every algebra. Since $n_r$ is a product in $U_r,U_{-r},U_r$, it follows in particular that $\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_b=X_b$ in the disconnected case, $\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_d=X_d$ in $B_2$, and $\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_f=X_f$ in $G_2$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.16, pp.140--142, and root lists of Isogeny Theorem Step 2, pp.205--206; agent-explicit applications of the empty commutator support.

proof.text:
We will use the following immediate consequence of the characterization in [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]. If $h$ is a word in $n_a,n_b$, its Weyl action carries a simple root $r$ to a simple root $s$, and $\operatorname{Ad}(h)X_r=X_s$, then $h n_r h^{-1}=n_s$. Indeed $h\exp_r(v)h^{-1}=\exp_s(\operatorname{Ad}(h)v)$: conjugating the map preserves its defining tangent inclusion and torus equivariance, so uniqueness identifies it. The same holds on the negative root. The image of the linked opposite generator is linked to $X_s$, because conjugating the displayed three-factor expression gives an element normalizing $T$. The uniqueness of the linked opposite generator therefore identifies it with $Y_{-s}$. Substitution in that three-factor expression gives the asserted equality in $G(A)$, rather than only equality of adjoint actions. Also, directly from $n_r^2=r^\vee(-1)$ and torus equivariance,
$$\operatorname{Ad}(n_r)^2Z=(-1)^{\langle c,r^\vee\rangle}Z\quad(Z\in\mathfrak g_c).$$

source.place: Corollary 5.1.9 and Remark 5.1.10, pp.132--133; canonical exponential characterization, Theorem 4.1.4. Agent-explicit use of uniqueness.

proof.text: For $A_1\times A_1$ take $h=n_a$, $r=s=b$. The reflections fix $b$, and step 2 gives $\operatorname{Ad}(h)X_b=X_b$. Step 3 implies $n_a n_b n_a^{-1}=n_b$, hence $n_a n_b=n_b n_a$. This is the required length-two equality.

source.place: Agent calculation from the disconnected rank-two list and Corollary 5.1.9; Isogeny Theorem Step 2, pp.205--206.

proof.text:
For $A_2$ put $c=a+b$ and $h=n_a n_b$. The seed gives $X_c=\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_a$ and $\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_b=-X_c$. Step 3 and $\langle b,a^\vee\rangle=-1$ give
$$\operatorname{Ad}(h)X_a=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_c=-\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)^2X_b=X_b.$$
The reflection formulas give $s_as_b(a)=b$. Thus step 3 gives $h n_a h^{-1}=n_b$. Multiplying by $h$ on the right yields $n_a n_b n_a=n_b n_a n_b$, as required.

source.place: Isogeny Theorem Step 2 (A2 normalization), Lemma 6.2.8, pp.205--207; agent-explicit word calculation.

proof.text:
For $B_2$ put $d=2a+b$, $X_d=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_b$ and $h=n_a n_b n_a$. Step 2 gives $\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_d=X_d$, and $\langle b,a^\vee\rangle=-2$ gives
$$\operatorname{Ad}(h)X_b=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_d=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)^2X_b=X_b.$$
The same root path is $b\mapsto d\mapsto d\mapsto b$, so $s_as_bs_a(b)=b$. Step 3 gives $h n_b=n_b h$, which expands to $n_a n_b n_a n_b=n_b n_a n_b n_a$.

source.place: Isogeny Theorem Step 2 (B2 normalization), pp.205--206; agent-explicit word calculation using no-sum commutation.

proof.text:
For $G_2$ put $e=3a+b$, $f=3a+2b$, $X_e=-\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_b$, $X_f=\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_e$, and $h=n_a n_b n_a n_b n_a$. Since $\langle b,a^\vee\rangle=-3$ and $\langle e,b^\vee\rangle=3(-1)+2=-1$, step 3 gives $\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_e=X_b$ and $\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_f=-X_e$. Step 2 gives $\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_f=X_f$. Reading the five factors of $h$ from right to left, the vector path is therefore
$$X_b\longmapsto-X_e\longmapsto-X_f\longmapsto-X_f\longmapsto X_e\longmapsto X_b.$$
The corresponding root path is $b,e,f,f,e,b$, so the Weyl action of $h$ fixes $b$. By step 3, $h n_b=n_b h$. Expanding gives precisely the length-six braid relation. Every minus sign is multiplication by the ring element $-1$, so the calculation also works in characteristics two and three.

source.place: Isogeny Theorem Step 2 (G2 signed vectors), pp.205--207; agent-explicit five-factor calculation.

proof.text: The four cases prove the equality in $G_J(A)$ and hence in $G(A)$ under the subgroup inclusion of step 1. For any homomorphism $A\to R$, the induced group homomorphism $G(A)\to G(R)$ sends both words to the corresponding words, because the canonical root exponentials commute with base change and the linked generator remains linked and is unique by [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]. Thus it sends the equality to the asserted base-changed equality. The zero ring gives the unique point over the empty scheme as well. All other calculations were identities over $A$ and used full torus characters; no passage to geometric points, reduction of $A$, central quotient, or division by an integer occurred.
